entry.title: Case-Sensitive and Case-Insensitive Match in Google Sheets
entry.summary: Most lookups in Google Sheets ignore capital letters, which is usually helpful and sometimes a problem. If "abc" and "ABC" are different codes, VLOOKUP will quietly return the wrong one. This page lists which functions ignore case, which respect it, and the formulas that force either behaviour. These treat "abc", "Abc" and "ABC" as the same: VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP and MATCH COUNTIF, COUNTIFS, SUMIF, SUMIFS The = operator: ="abc"="ABC" returns TRUE SEARCH (but see below for FIND) EXACT(a, b) returns TRUE only when the text is identical, including case. FIND(find, in) is case-sensitive: =FIND("ab","xAbc") gives #VALUE!, while =FIND("Ab","xAbc") gives 2. SEARCH does the same job ignoring case: =SEARCH("ab","xAbc") gives 2. REGEXMATCH is case-sensitive by default: =REGEXMATCH("Abc","abc") is FALSE. …

entry.title: Ghostscript's font bug reached 10 apps through a `.png`
entry.summary:
Ghostscript's font bug reached 10 apps through a .png
A file named .png that contains PostScript can reach Ghostscript from ten different applications — and a use-after-free in Ghostscript's Type 1 font loader turns that into remote code execution, past the -dSAFER sandbox. CVE-2026-125396, published November 9. Pre-auth RCE was confirmed against Debian 13's CUPS, Roundcube, WordPress, and Google's own document pipeline. The writeup is from pwn.ai ("How We Hacked the Pipes"), and it is unusually complete. The flaw is in .putgstringcopy, a helper in Ghostscript's Resource/Init/gs_fonts.ps that loads Type 1 fonts. Ghostscript implements parts of its own font loading in PostScript, and this helper needed to write into protected font dictionaries, so it used an internal operation called .for…

entry.title: Fitting a model checker into one million compiler steps
entry.summary: An escrow contract has five actions: Deposit, Lock, Release, Refund, Dispute. Unit tests check the sequences somebody thought of. The bug that drains it is usually the sequence nobody wrote a test for. So I made the compiler try all of them. In exhaust, fe build runs a breadth-first search over every reachable state of the escrow's state machine, checks five invariants on every state and every transition, and refuses to compile if one breaks. The search has to finish inside a hard wall: Fe 26.6.0 gives each static_assert 1,000,000 evaluator steps and a recursion limit of 64. This post is about fitting a model checker under that ceiling.
